why: Referent correction on the always-on subagent guard claim. The note records why; the claim text itself changed past the 400-char prefix, which claim-drift caught and rekey could not.

changes.to: Added 2026-08-18, Tier 1. Four of the five skills.md gaps; the fifth, phase-agent-names-primary-and-secondary-references, is DEFERRED to the dispatch-prompt section in subagents.md, which does not exist yet, because its own note says it merges there and writing it here would separate it from its three siblings. The always-on subagent guard is the sharpest of the four: both mechanisms are documented and neither is usable for an always-on routing skill, so the convention fills a real hole. CORRECTED 2026-08-18: the closing clause read "A live instance runs in this project", which was wrong. An independent review flagged it as unverified; re-verification found the pattern ships in the superpowers plugin (using-superpowers/SKILL.md, guard first in the body) and that SUBAGENT-STOP occurs zero times across all 30 files of this library, positive control 30 of 30 on "claude". The mechanism half of the claim was never in doubt; only the referent was.
